topic: Comparison of nucleic acid simulation software

findings.summary: Nucleic acid simulation software encompasses tools for molecular dynamics, Monte Carlo sampling, and coarse-grained modeling of DNA and RNA. These programs vary in their treatment of explicit or implicit solvent, force fields, and hardware acceleration. Many support model building and 3D visualization, while specialized tools address ligand interactions, replica exchange, and refinement of nucleic acid structures. Licensing ranges from free and open-source to proprietary, with capabilities spanning from coarse-grained biophysics to all-atom dynamics.

mechanisms.title: Molecular dynamics and force fields
mechanisms.explanation: Software such as AMBER, CHARMM, NAMD, and CP2K perform all-atom molecular dynamics simulations of nucleic acids using physics-based force fields. These models compute forces and integrate equations of motion to simulate the time evolution of DNA and RNA structures, often supporting explicit water models and GPU acceleration for performance.

mechanisms.title: Coarse-grained modeling and RNA folding
mechanisms.explanation: Tools like oxDNA, SimRNA, and MDynaMix employ coarse-grained representations to simulate nucleic acid thermodynamics and folding. These methods reduce atomic detail to capture sequence-dependent behavior, enable large-scale conformational changes, and facilitate RNA 3D structure prediction and docking.

unknowns: Exact parameterization differences between force fields for diverse nucleic acid types
Whether implicit solvent models accurately capture specific water-mediated nucleic acid interactions
The degree to which GPU acceleration affects numerical stability in long-timescale nucleic acid simulations
How replica exchange mechanisms are configured for nucleic acid-specific energy landscapes
